summary.text: 过 means “to pass” or “go across.” Its traditional form 過 is analyzed as 辵, a movement element, plus 咼, a sound element. The simplified graph has been used as a variant for centuries, though its precise graphic route is unresolved.

formation.text: The received analysis of 過 is phonosemantic: 辵 contributes movement, while 咼 provides a sound cue. This is a historical dictionary analysis, not proof of the graph’s earliest composition.

components.text: In 過, 辶 is the conventional left-side form of 辵 and contributes the idea of movement. These are side and full forms, not evidence of a chronological change.
過 uses 咼 as its sound element. Reconstructions suggest a related, though not exact, sound; accounts of 咼’s internal shape and original referent remain disputed.

sound.text: In Zhengzhang Shangfang Old Chinese, 咼 *kʰʷroːl and 過 *kloːl or *kloːls have similar but nonidentical reconstructed sounds, supporting a proposed phonetic relationship.

history.text: The seal-script-style 過 illustrates the form transmitted in the Shuowen tradition, analyzed as 辵 plus 咼. The image is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact, and does not establish the graph’s earliest composition.

A secondary account reports an oracle-bone form 𨒵 analyzed as 辵 plus 冎, but this proposal has not been verified from primary inscription images. The earliest form and the internal history of 咼 remain unsettled.

过 is documented as a long-used common variant of 過 in later popular texts and was listed as its simplified form in the 1964 table. Although a cursive origin has been proposed, the precise graphic route is unresolved.

uncertainties.text: The 辵-plus-咼 analysis is a received historical interpretation. The earliest composition and the original referent, if any, of 咼’s internal shape remain unresolved.
The proposed phonetic relationship rests on Zhengzhang Shangfang reconstructions that differ in details; values from other reconstruction systems have not been independently confirmed here.
The precise graphic route from 過 to 过 is unclear, although earlier variant use and later official standardization are documented.

senses.text: The received Shuowen entry glosses 過 as 度也, interpreted as measuring or crossing a distance. The date of the earliest use is unresolved.
Classical citations show 過 used to mean “exceed,” but do not date the emergence of this sense.
A later commentary interprets “fault” or “error” as an extension of the passing sense. The timing and precise path of that development are unresolved.
The common current meaning includes passing, passing through, and going across.

developments.text: A historical commentary treats “fault” or “error” as an extension of “passing,” though it does not establish when or exactly how the change occurred.

limitations.text: Dictionary examples also record senses such as visiting, excessive degree, and an experiential or completive particle, but do not date their emergence or establish a sequence connecting them.
The dictionary tradition records distinct level-tone and departing-tone readings, but does not date their separation or establish a separate semantic development.

overview.text: 过 means “to pass” or “go across.” Its traditional form 過 combines a movement element with 咼 as a proposed sound element. The simplified form has long served as a variant, though its precise graphic route is unclear.

components.text: 辶 is the conventional left-side form of 辵 and contributes movement in 過.
咼 is the proposed sound element in 過; its reconstructed sound resembles, but does not exactly match, the character’s.

relationships.text: In 過, 辶 is the side form of 辵 and contributes movement in the received analysis.
過 is analyzed with 咼 as a phonetic element; same-system reconstructions are related but not identical.
过 is documented as a long-used common variant of 過; its precise graphic route is unresolved.
